invariant: PlantUML establishes the unscaled root viewport as an integer visible frontier before applying dpi or an explicit document scale. TextBlockExporter supplies the double final dimension to SvgGraphics, whose constructor calls ensureVisible and stores floor(dimension + 1) in integer maxX/maxY. SvgGraphics then multiplies those integer frontiers by the document scale: exact width/height attributes use the scaled decimal value, while style and viewBox use the truncated scaled integer. Rust must preserve that ordering independently of the full precision retained for element coordinates.
causal_divergence: Rust's uniform-scale path renders the whole base SVG under plantuml_metrics::with_full_precision and then scales the finished root attributes. A controlled component input with explicit root Margin 10, root Padding 6, global skinparam Padding 5, and Verdana 12 is exact at dpi 96. Changing only dpi to 100 leaves every entity, edge, label, height, and paint attribute exact but makes Rust scale a 162px base width to 168.75px where Java scales its ensureVisible frontier 163px to 169.7917px. The four remaining Cerulean, Minty, Superhero, and United component failures have the same root-only signature and all four themes set dpi 100. Margin-only values 2, 5, and 10 and the same font/padding axes at dpi 96 are exact, excluding component geometry and margin constants as the cause.
planned_change: Separate root-frontier integerization from element-coordinate precision in the scaled render path. Establish the base root width and height with the same integer visible-frontier semantics as an ordinary unscaled render and Java SvgGraphics.ensureVisible, then scale those integer roots while retaining full precision for path, shape, text, and style geometry. Keep width/height decimal formatting and style/viewBox truncation in scale_svg_numbers. The correction must be derived from the rendered base frontier, not from diagram family, theme name, fixture dimensions, or a blanket increment.
perturbation_axes: dpi 96, 100, 125, and 150 versus explicit fractional scale directives
base dimensions immediately below, exactly on, and immediately above integer frontiers
component, class, usecase, and state diagram families
explicit document margins 0, 2, 5, and 10 with asymmetric four-side controls
font family/size and global padding changed independently
top-to-bottom versus left-to-right topology and renamed labels
scope_boundary: This mechanism owns only root SVG base-frontier integerization before uniform scaling. It does not alter element coordinates, font metrics, layout, document margin resolution, arc command roles, XML token boundaries, comparator behavior, fixture eligibility, or family baselines.
acceptance: The four themed component golden failures become exact through diff_one --no-oracle with no interior SVG change.
The controlled dpi-only pair proves that dpi 96 and dpi 100 use the same integer base frontier before scaling.
Fresh Java perturbations cover at least two diagram families, boundary positions, scale forms, margins, fonts, and topology axes.
Existing exact scaled diagrams and fit-to-box behavior do not regress.
An independent checker audits this account and implementation at exact revisions and preserves every passing or failing perturbation.
forbidden_approaches: adding one pixel to every scaled SVG root or keying a correction to dpi 100
matching theme names, component labels, fixture paths, or known root dimensions
rounding element geometry early to make root dimensions fit
changing comparator tolerance, baselines, skip markers, or fixture eligibility
